title: Emrys and the Border
premise: Isandro Montrose, a disgraced intelligence analyst living off-grid in a border town, discovers that Flight 447—a charter carrying a whistleblower and evidence of a private surveillance consortium's crimes—has been erased from every record while still airborne. As the consortium's cleaners close in and a global summit approaches where the consortium will be granted legal immunity, Isandro realizes his own erased past was no accident: he was their prototype, a man memory-wiped and reinserted into civilian life. To survive, he must recover what he buried in his own mind—the access key to the consortium's ledger—and decide whether to trade it for his life or detonate it publicly before the summit convenes. In the end, Isandro broadcasts the ledger at the cost of his cover identity, walking away as a stranger even to himself, but free.
about_author: Mirabel Ashgrove is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent years adjacent to the world of classified contracting before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Isandro Montrose's POV. We meet him in the border town of Puerto Cielo: three agencies have discarded him, he keeps a packed bag under the bed, and he rehearses his cover story nightly at a bar called the Halfway House. The emotional beat is brittle calm—routine as armor—until a stranger asks one question too many about his past.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A former colleague, Dana Okafor, calls from a burner: she's on charter Flight 447 inbound with documents that can sink the Halcyon Consortium before the summit grants it immunity. Mid-call, her voice cuts out—and every trace of the flight vanishes from arrival boards, databases, even Isandro's own call log. Beat: dread crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He confirms the wipe isn't a glitch: air traffic tapes, weather logs, even a fisherman's photo of the contrail are gone or altered. Local police chief Reyes warns him to drop it. The beat is gaslighting made physical—Isandro doubting his own memory until he finds a paper ticket stub Dana mailed days earlier.

chapters.title: The Stub
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The envelope contains a boarding pass and a note in Dana's handwriting: 'Ask yourself why you left.' It triggers a fragment of buried memory—a white room, a voice counting backward. First hint that his firing from three agencies was orchestrated. Beat: vertigo; the hunter realizing he was always the quarry.

chapters.title: Halfway House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Mara Voss, Halcyon's fixer, arrives in Puerto Cielo posing as an insurance investigator. She interviews the bar owner and quietly maps Isandro's routines. Her chapters reveal cold professional competence laced with private doubt. Beat: menace entering through politeness.

chapters.title: Three Firings
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He pulls his own personnel files through old contacts and finds inconsistencies: dates that don't match his memories, supervisors who don't recall him. A retired archivist hints at a program called LANTERN—behavioral erasure for burned assets. Beat: grief for a self he may never have known.

chapters.title: The Wreck in the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with a brief interlude from a dying Halcyon pilot. Following the flight path, Isandro finds Flight 447's wreckage hidden in a dry lakebed, stripped of its black boxes—but not of bodies. Dana's seat is empty. Beat: horror tempered by hope; she may have parachuted.

chapters.title: Voss Makes Contact
chapters.summary: Mara Voss's POV. She offers Isandro a clean exit: walk away, keep his new name, and Halcyon forgets him. He stalls, buying time, and notices she flinches at the word 'LANTERN'—she has history with the program too. Beat: two liars circling, each sensing a crack in the other.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Dana surfaces, injured and hiding with a smuggler network along the border river. She reveals the ledger's access key isn't a drive—it's encoded in the memory of the analyst who vetted it. Isandro. His 'burnout' was a containment operation. Beat: betrayal curdling into fury.

chapters.title: LANTERN
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. She explains the program: Halcyon wipes inconvenient witnesses and reinserts them as controlled civilians. Isandro was their success story—until residual memory began leaking. The summit in nine days will grant Halcyon sovereign immunity, making erasure permanent and legal. Beat: a ticking clock bolted to a personal wound.

chapters.title: Chief Reyes's Choice
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The police chief, who has taken Halcyon money for years, must choose between protecting his town and protecting himself. He tips off Voss about the river safehouse but keeps one detail back—his conscience priced, not sold. Beat: complicity and its small rebellions.

chapters.title: River Crossing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A night extraction of Dana goes wrong when Voss's team hits the safehouse early. Isandro and Dana escape through the marshes; the smuggler Tavo dies covering them. Beat: survival purchased with someone else's life—the book's central theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The White Room
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, intercut with recovered memory fragments. Under Dana's guidance and a risky drug protocol, Isandro descends into suppressed recollections: the lab, the chair, the voice counting down—and his own hand signing consent. He volunteered, once, to protect someone. Beat: the past arriving like floodwater.

chapters.title: The Person He Protected
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The recovered memory names his daughter, Elena—officially dead in the accident that 'broke' him, actually alive and hidden by Halcyon as leverage. Dana confirms it. Now the trade is explicit: the key for Elena's safety. Beat: love weaponized; the price of survival given a face.

chapters.title: Summit City
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs converge. Isandro and Dana travel to the capital under forged papers while Voss reports upward to Halcyon director Aurel Kade, who orders the summit venue prepped for one final erasure. Beat: converging vectors, the net tightening around everyone.

chapters.title: Kade's Offer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Captured during a decoy meeting, Isandro faces Kade, who offers everything—Elena, a new life, even restored memories—in exchange for the key delivered quietly. Kade is reasonable, almost kind, which makes him monstrous. Beat: temptation at its most articulate.

chapters.title: Voss's Crack
chapters.summary: Mara Voss's POV. Ordered to prepare Isandro for a second, deeper wipe, Voss discovers her own file in the LANTERN archive—she was wiped twice already. She defects, springing Isandro, choosing a painful truth over a managed lie. Beat: the corrupt system consuming its own.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Isandro, Dana, and Voss plan the broadcast: the ledger key must be entered physically at the summit's secure terminal before immunity votes close. They rehearse, argue, and reckon with odds none of them like. Beat: the quiet before the storm, alliances sealed in exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Summit Floor
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Disguised as catering security, Isandro penetrates the summit while Voss triggers a diversion and Dana feeds the press a partial leak. Kade senses the trap and locks down the floor. Beat: high-wire tension, every exit narrowing.

chapters.title: The Key
chapters.summary: Climax. Isandro reaches the terminal; Kade holds Elena on a live feed as leverage. Isandro enters the key anyway, broadcasting the ledger globally, and Kade's empire begins collapsing in real time. Voss takes a bullet shielding Isandro; Kade is arrested by his own security once immunity evaporates. Beat: sacrifice over bargain.

chapters.title: Afterimages
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the aftermath, Elena chooses her guardians and her own name rather than return to a father who is partly a stranger. Dana offers him a place in the oversight commission; he declines. Beat: bittersweet reckoning—victory that doesn't restore what was taken.

chapters.title: A New Name, Packed Light
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Isandro's POV. Months later, in another border town, Isandro unpacks the go-bag at last and hangs up a coat as if staying. He receives a postcard from Elena—one line, no return address—and smiles. Final beat: survival's true price paid, and worth it; invisibility traded for a self he chose.
